entry.title: Diffuse supernova background
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The Super-Kamiokande Collaboration reported an indication of electron antineutrinos from the diffuse supernova neutrino background, from a spectral fit of a 5003.0-day dataset. The analysis has better rejection of atmospheric-neutrino backgrounds, updated systematic uncertainties and a refined spectral fit. For a representative DSNB model the best-fit flux was 3.6 (+1.6, −1.5) cm^-2 s^-1 above 13.3 MeV, a 2.6σ tension with the null hypothesis. Models with different spectral shapes gave similar significances.

entry.title: KM3NeT construction and status
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. KM3NeT reports that Cable Termination Frame 3 was installed at the ARCA deep-sea site during a marine campaign by Alcatel Submarine Networks. The collaboration describes two further steps for ARCA and ORCA in the same period. It has also been recognised as a Landmark in the ESFRI Roadmap 2026, and held its Autumn 2026 Collaboration Meeting in Siracusa.

entry.title: IceCube at the Pole
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. KM3NeT congratulated Francis Halzen on the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics, awarded for his contributions to IceCube and the discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos. The weekly Pole reports describe the station gathering at the IceCube Lab to mark the award. In the following week the winterovers replaced a hard drive, applied software updates, and carried out calibration operations on the Upgrade.

entry.title: IceCube data, X-ray transients
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. An analysis of 14 years of publicly available IceCube muon-track data looked for neutrinos from 27 fast X-ray transients detected by Einstein Probe. It used the unbinned maximum-likelihood method of IceCube point-source searches. No statistically significant excess was found; the largest TS was 4.77, for EP240801a, with a local p-value of 0.04. The authors therefore set 90% confidence-level upper limits on the differential muon-neutrino flux.

entry.title: Neutrinos and gravitational waves
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The ANTARES and KM3NeT Collaborations present two searches combining LIGO-Virgo gravitational-wave data from the third observing run with ANTARES and ORCA neutrino data. In the first, selected high-energy neutrino candidates serve as triggers to search for gravitational-wave candidates. The second looks for spatial and temporal coincidences involving subthreshold candidates.

entry.title: Baikal-GVD
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Baikal-GVD, a cubic-kilometre detector in Lake Baikal, is 70% complete and has taken data in partial configurations since 2016. A point-source search on a 5-year track-like dataset from 2019-2024 found no significant source. Upper limits are given for selected candidate objects and compared with published IceCube, ANTARES and KM3NeT results.

entry.title: T2K near detector upgrade
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. SuperFGD, a key component of the ND280 upgrade, is a segmented plastic scintillator made of about 2 million optically isolated 1 cm^3 cubes read out by three orthogonal wavelength-shifting fibres. It gives 3D images of neutrino interactions, detects protons down to a threshold of about 300 MeV/c, identifies Michel electrons and can measure neutron energy by time of flight. The paper reports its performance in the T2K beam.

entry.title: PUEO balloon mission
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The PUEO Collaboration describes the design and flight of a balloon-borne antenna array built to detect the Askaryan emission from ultrahigh-energy neutrino interactions. Such neutrinos are expected from ultrahigh-energy cosmic-ray sources, and their low flux requires very large detector volumes.

entry.title: PBR and KM3-230213A
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. POEMMA-Balloon with Radio (PBR) is a pathfinder for a future POEMMA mission, planned to fly on a super-pressure balloon in Spring 2028. A new study evaluates its sensitivity to a boosted dark matter scenario proposed as an explanation of the KM3NeT muon event of 120 (+110, −60) PeV.

entry.title: The paper computes the neutrino emissivity of Δ-direct-Urca processes in neutron stars, where Δ isobars appear
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper computes the neutrino emissivity of Δ-direct-Urca processes in neutron stars, where Δ isobars appear alongside nucleons and hyperons. Nucleonic and hyperonic Urca processes are established as dominant neutron-star cooling mechanisms, and the Δ contribution had not been evaluated explicitly. It is relevant to anyone using neutrino emission to model neutron-star thermal evolution.

entry.title: The paper proves a no-go theorem: any completely positive, trace-preserving evolution covariant under rotation
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper proves a no-go theorem: any completely positive, trace-preserving evolution covariant under rotations of the mass-coherence plane is exactly blind to a Majorana phase in two-flavour oscillations. A rate anisotropy in the decoherence can supply an environmental phase reference. This sets the conditions under which open-system effects could reveal a Majorana phase.

entry.title: The authors calculate two-neutrino double-beta decay rates without decoupling nuclear structure from the lepto
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors calculate two-neutrino double-beta decay rates without decoupling nuclear structure from the lepton kinematics, and compare with closure, non-closure and Taylor-expansion approximations for 82Se and 136Xe. They report deviations in the rates and electron spectra relative to these methods. This bears on the accuracy of the standard treatment of two-neutrino double-beta decay.

entry.title: The paper studies a gauged U(1) L_mu − L_tau model with an ultralight vector boson that kinetically mixes with
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper studies a gauged U(1) L_mu − L_tau model with an ultralight vector boson that kinetically mixes with the photon and adds a matter potential in the Sun, modifying MSW oscillations. It uses solar neutrino measurements from Borexino, SNO and Super-Kamiokande and discusses prospects for JUNO and XLZD. It shows how solar neutrinos can constrain such light mediators.

entry.title: The authors assess whether neutrinos from past Galactic core-collapse supernovae could be detected as nuclear
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors assess whether neutrinos from past Galactic core-collapse supernovae could be detected as nuclear recoil tracks in ancient minerals (paleodetectors). They vary neutron-star masses, include failed supernovae that form black holes, and consider the nuclear equation of state. They find the sensitivity is enhanced for models with larger neutrino emission.

entry.title: The paper studies neutrino mass and thermal leptogenesis in the Babu-Nandi-Tavartkiladze model, with a scalar
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper studies neutrino mass and thermal leptogenesis in the Babu-Nandi-Tavartkiladze model, with a scalar quadruplet and a pair of vectorlike fermion triplets. Neutrino masses arise from a dimension-7 operator at tree level and a dimension-5 operator at one loop, accommodating sub-eV masses with new physics at the TeV scale. Leptogenesis here differs from the canonical seesaw case.
